failure_summary.description: A name-only prompt left the relation implicit, and the agent supplied an office title rather than the expected associated country.
Mechanical singular agreement changed a conventional plural-form instrument name into the singular.

patch.reasoning: The name-only prompt does not establish a reliably generalizable relation, so adding a rule to infer one risks repeating an ineffective broad heuristic. The number mismatch exposes a specific weakness in the current instruction to match grammatical number: canonical labels can be plural even for one instrument.

edits.target: For definition clues, give the requested category term rather than a list of examples, and match grammatical number and necessary articles.
edits.content: For definition clues, give the requested category term rather than a list of examples. Use the conventional canonical headword or name form supported by the directly relevant clue or source, including established plural-form labels even when referring to one instrument or category; do not mechanically singularize or pluralize for agreement. Include an article only when grammatically required.
